clauses.reason: Section 1 directs the Secretary of State (for the Foreign Service personnel and retirement systems) and the Director of the United States Information Agency (for that agency's Foreign Service personnel system) to promulgate policies and related regulations after consultation with the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission. EO 12292 (signed 1981-02-23; 46 FR 13967, Federal Register of February 25, 1981), Sec. 10(i), revokes "Sections 1, 3, and 5 of Executive Order No. 11434 of November 8,1968;", and Sec. 11 says "This Order shall be effective as of February 15,1981." The revocation is therefore recorded as effective 1981-02-15, the stated effective date, not the signing date 1981-02-23. Sec. 10(i) names this section expressly. EO 12107 (Dec. 28, 1978) amended the references to the Civil Service Commission; that amendment does not end the section and is listed as a later event. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; Federal Register of March 3, 1986, Vol. 51, No. 41) revokes EO 11434 together with "any amendments thereto"; it is recorded as the formal disposition and is listed as a later event, but it is dated after this clause had ended and is not the first end.

clauses.reason: Section 2 provides that the Board of the Foreign Service and the Board of Examiners for the Foreign Service, established by EO 11264, shall exercise for Foreign Service information officers the functions that order delegated to them for Foreign Service officers, and that the Boards shall perform such further functions for United States Information Agency personnel as the Director may delegate. EO 12292 Sec. 10(i) revoked only Sections 1, 3 and 5 of EO 11434, so Section 2 survived that order, although Sec. 10(h) revoked Part III of EO 11264 (the Board of Examiners) effective 1981-02-15; that partial revocation reaches half of what Section 2 refers to and is listed as a later event. The Board of the Foreign Service (Part II of EO 11264) continued, and Section 2 with it, until EO 12363 (signed 1982-05-21; 47 FR 22497, Federal Register of May 25, 1982) said in its Sec. 3: "Executive Order No. 11264 of December 31, 1965, as amended, is revoked." EO 12363 states no later effective date, so the end is recorded as its signing date, 1982-05-21. Section 2 has no object once EO 11264, the instrument that established both Boards and delegated the functions Section 2 extends, was revoked in its entirety. No held source shows Section 2 extinguished earlier by the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (effective 1981-02-15): EO 12292, the order that conformed existing orders to that Act, left Sections 2 and 4 of EO 11434 unrevoked. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; Federal Register of March 3, 1986, Vol. 51, No. 41) revokes EO 11434 together with "any amendments thereto"; it is recorded as the formal disposition and is listed as a later event, but it is dated after this clause had ended and is not the first end.

clauses.reason: Section 4 amends Section 21 of EO 11264: it deletes the United States Information Agency from the list in subsection (b)(2), adds a new paragraph (b)(3) for two United States Information Agency officials designated by the Director, and conforms subsection (d). Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling (2026-10-21) an amending clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends. The parent here is Section 21 of EO 11264 (Part II, the Board of the Foreign Service), which EO 12292 did not revoke (Sec. 10(h) revoked only Part III); Section 4 of EO 11434 was left unrevoked by Sec. 10(i). EO 12363 (signed 1982-05-21; 47 FR 22497) said in its Sec. 3: "Executive Order No. 11264 of December 31, 1965, as amended, is revoked." and states no later effective date, so the end is recorded as 1982-05-21. The amendment is a rewrite of part of a section that no longer existed after that date, and the Board it concerned was replaced by the Board of the Foreign Service established by Sec. 9 of EO 12293, as added by Sec. 1 of EO 12363. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; Federal Register of March 3, 1986, Vol. 51, No. 41) revokes EO 11434 together with "any amendments thereto"; it is recorded as the formal disposition and is listed as a later event, but it is dated after this clause had ended and is not the first end.

The revocation is therefore recorded as effective 1981-02-15, the stated effective date, not the signing date 1981-02-23. conflict_resolutions.FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT: The two readings concern different instruments. EO 12292 Sec. 10(i) ends EO 11434 only in part (Sections 1, 3 and 5, as it says by number), and Sec. 10(h) revokes only Part III of EO 11264. EO 12363 Sec. 3 revokes EO 11264 as amended in its entirety, and reaches EO 11434 only through that parent order: it ends Sections 2 and 4, which operate only on EO 11264, and does not touch Sections 1, 3 and 5, which had ended already. The claim uses each instrument for the sections it reaches.

research_rationale:
EO 11434 (signed 1968-11-08; 33 FR 16485, Federal Register of November 13, 1968) deals with the administration of the Foreign Service personnel systems: policies and regulations (Sec. 1), the Boards established by EO 11264 (Sec. 2), the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System (Sec. 3), an amendment of Section 21 of EO 11264 (Sec. 4) and its effective date (Sec. 5). EO 12292 (effective as of 1981-02-15) revoked Sections 1, 3 and 5; Sections 2 and 4 survived until EO 12363 revoked EO 11264 on 1982-05-21, which is the latest first end and so the whole-order end. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is the later formal revocation. The held OFR notes "Revoked in part by: EO 12292" and "Revoked by: EO 12553" are both reconciled in this claim, and EO 12107 (amendment) is a later event.

savings.reason: Neither EO 12292 nor EO 12363 contains a savings clause for EO 11434 (the held texts of both contain no "remain in effect", "continue in effect" or similar wording). Sections 1, 3 and 5 only assigned policy-making and regulation-making duties and a delegation, and Sections 2 and 4 concerned boards of an order that was itself revoked; none created property, rights or functions that survive the revocations, and regulations issued under them are completed acts, not continuing commands of this order.
